status: Finite phase-space/PDF-evolution mismatch is quantitatively validated for a central u-ubar DY point; full-ensemble and heavy-flavour attribution remains incomplete.

expected_relation.derivation: If dlog(f_a)/dlog(t)=R_backward(t)-V_a(t), then integrating gives this relation. It requires common real/virtual kernels, scale arguments, regulator and phase-space bounds.
expected_relation.failure: Ordinary DGLAP PDFs include real evolution up to z=1, whereas a finite-mass kT-ordered shower has z<Z(t)<1. Multiplying by the ordinary PDF ratio does not undo this mismatch.

primary_sources.title: MC@NLO-Delta paper
anchors: Appendix A, footnote 28 explicitly references Nagy/Soper PDF-property concerns
Eqs.A.10-A.17 show forward prescriptions equal through logarithm and constant, differing in O(epsilon)
epsilon is roughly pT/mdip, and an interval q->Q near the hard scale need not have small epsilon throughout

primary_sources.title: Nagy and Soper, Evolution of parton showers and parton distribution functions
anchors: Eq.4-7 derive the PDF property while neglecting finite z bounds
Section IV tests Pythia DY and explains why the upper z bound matters
The published example uses high-mass large-x DY; it is evidence for the mechanism, not a numerical prediction for this low-mass sample

boundary_identity: Dlog(f)/Dlog(t)+alphaS*V1/(2*pi)-R_backward = alphaS/(2*pi)*{CF*Z*(1-Z) + integral_Z^1 dz Pqq(z)[xfq(x/z)/xfq(x)-1] + integral_Z^1 dz Pqg(z)*xfg(x/z)/xfq(x)}, Z=zmax; assuming LO DGLAP evolution

independent_shower_check.source: Parent-agent independently generated exact central Born point with all matched historical settings; result file recorded separately in the same audit directory.

kernel_implementation_findings: No obvious missing half or doubled colour factor was found for light incoming quarks.
Forward mode1 correctly combines Pqq and Pgq with z weighting. For a massless quark this gives integrand CF*(2/(1-z)-3*z).

The code retains a random forward off-diagonal sister flavour, which can introduce heavy sister masses; this is omitted in the illustrative integral. Fresh API agreement bounds its importance at the chosen point.
The quark forward logic is already present in the historical8.225 tree; no new8.313 coefficient discrepancy was identified.

ranked_causes.cause: Finite-z mismatch between full PDF scale evolution and phase-space-limited backward shower
ranked_causes.evidence: Independent kernel quadrature reproduces the observed central-light-quark deficit curve very closely; omitted g->q feed dominates the exponent.
ranked_causes.confidence: Strong: an independent100000-trial exact-point shower agrees with the truncated-kernel prediction at allsix testedcuts within1.9sigma.

ranked_causes.evidence: Fresh-forward rate .8689985 versus stored .8625544 per quark at q20 contributes about1.5% to a two-leg probability, much smaller than the main discrepancy.
ranked_causes.confidence: Measured small contribution at this point

ranked_causes.cause: Heavy-flavour thresholds, valence/sea PDF handling, PDF interpolation/QED evolution
ranked_causes.evidence: They can explain flavour-dependent residuals and differences from the massless total-PDF rate; not needed for the centralu/d deficit.
ranked_causes.confidence: Subleading candidates not separately quantified across the ensemble

what_is_not_proven: The finite-boundary integral is an illustrative single Born point, not an integration over all1000 Born states.
A precise separation of every remaining percent among sister-mass effects, valence/sea selection and interpolation is not done.
Numerically successful mode0/mode2 replacements do not by themselves fix the forward-table plus PDF contract.
